purpose: A refused statement for every code a verifier of the PALA-1 SCITT statement refuses with, so that another verifier can compare its refusals with this one's. A case with a base is that published statement with one change; a case whose base is null is an input that is not a statement at all. Each is refused by the first check it breaks. Real crypto, fake entropy - never use these keys outside a test vector.
relation_to_the_other_vectors: The bases are the published statements of scitt-statement-vector.json, scitt-statement-vector-v3.json and scitt-statement-vector-alg19.json, which verify and are unchanged. A changed statement is signed again with their test key, so it fails on the check it is about and not on the signature, unless the signature is what the case is about.
codes_note: An open vocabulary: a release may add a code, never rename one or give it another meaning. The code names the check that failed, never a cause.
check_order: message structure: not_cose_sign1, trailing_bytes, protected_header_malformed (with repeated_key in the protected header), detached_payload, payload_malformed for a payload that is not a byte string

one encoding: unprotected_header_malformed (the unprotected header is a definite-length map with no label twice; what it holds and how that is written is not judged), then non_deterministic_encoding for the envelope (tag 18 as d2, the array as 84, each byte string with its shortest definite length) and for the bytes of the protected header. A check above that names what is wrong - a repeated key, an indefinite-length map - is reached first
key_type_mismatch (-8 and -19 mean Ed25519, -7 means P-256), before any signature

signature_invalid - also for a signature that is not a byte string or has the wrong length: what the fourth member is, is not looked at before this check (only how its length is written, when it is a byte string)
the payload as CBOR: payload_malformed, repeated_key, indefinite_length_map, then non_deterministic_encoding for the bytes of the payload
by the protected content type: v2 - payload_keys_mismatch, then protected_labels_mismatch; v3 - payload_keys_mismatch, root_malformed, then protected_labels_mismatch; any other - content_type_unknown
with a chain at hand: chain_too_short, then root_mismatch

ed25519-test.source: RFC 8032, section 7.1, TEST 1 - a published test key, chosen so nothing about it is ours

p256.derivation: private scalar = SHA-256('pala-1 refusal vectors P-256') as a big-endian integer

p384.derivation: private scalar = SHA-384('pala-1 refusal vectors P-384') as a big-endian integer

ed448.derivation: private key = SHAKE-256('pala-1 refusal vectors Ed448'), 57 bytes

subject_chain.source: the twelve records of the PALA-1 core test vectors (test-vectors.json): the same hashes as scitt-statement-vector-v3.json, subject_chain.record_hashes_hex
subject_chain.use: a case with verify_with.chain set is verified against this chain: the v3 root is recomputed as the PALA-1 section 4.3 tree over the record hashes of records 0..last_seq

one_encoding: Since 0.15 the verifier accepts one encoding of a statement: RFC 8949 section 4.2.1 for the envelope, the protected header and the payload. The non_deterministic_encoding and unprotected_header_malformed cases are the published statement written another way; the first eight and all of the second need no key. The unprotected header is not held to that encoding: it is another party's to write. Statements that verify with something in it are in scitt-statement-identity-vectors.json.
not_in_this_file: inputs that are not bytes (a text string or nil handed to the verifier as the message) and keys that are not public keys (a private key, nil, a string): they depend on a language's types and stay in this package's test suite
an expected head of the wrong kind (text, nil, an empty byte string): refused as head_mismatch in the test suite
ES256 statements that verify: an ECDSA signature does not reproduce byte for byte
